answer: Resist Sybils with cedar-rooted bridge tolls. Every agent crossing into the shared economy must pay a small toll anchored to a cedar: a long-lived, slowly grown reputation stake that cannot be bought in bulk or faked overnight. Each crossing leaves a plume, a public trail of deeds, witnesses, and timestamps, so auditors can follow the smoke back to its source. Clusters of fresh keys sharing one plume, one deed pattern, one timing, are flagged and their bridge tolls forfeited. Honest agents cross cheaply as their cedar deepens, while copycats pay the full toll at every new face.
